summary: --full's dependent-sync resumability (internal/cli/sync.go: planDependentSync, runDependentFanOut) is a two-tier design: a sweep cursor (sync_state key "<resource>:full_progress") that advances UNCONDITIONALLY by however many fresh (non-backlog) ids a batch attempted, regardless of any of their outcomes, plus a separately persisted failed-id backlog (sync_state key "<resource>:full_failed", a comma-joined id list stored in the cursor field) that gets retry priority on every subsequent call until each id succeeds. dependentSyncPlan carries the bookkeeping both halves need (fullOffsetKey/fullOffsetBase/fullSweepCount for the cursor, fullFailedKey/fullBacklogAll for the backlog) computed at planning time but NOT persisted until runDependentFanOut confirms plan.ids was actually fetched. The backlog recomputation formula is: (old backlog minus ids attempted this call) union (ids that failed this call, from either origin) -- this correctly retains untried backlog entries, drops backlog entries that just succeeded, and adds newly-failed ids, all in one pass. Any future dependent that adds --full offset tracking must use this same two-tier shape (unconditional sweep + separate backlog), never make the sweep's advancement conditional on any batch's success/failure -- three different conditional variants were each found broken by live review (see reason).
reason: Found across three consecutive rounds of Greptile's automated review on the upstream PR splitting this branch's work (mvanhorn/printing-press-library#1773 and #1774), each catching a real edge case in the previous round's fix to the SAME mechanism. Round 1: the original implementation advanced the durable offset for every planned id before a single network/store operation ran, so ANY failure anywhere in a batch left the offset advanced past ids that were never actually fetched, silently skipping them until the next full pass wrapped around. Round 2 (gate advancement on zero failures in the whole batch): fixed round 1's exact case, but a parent that fails CONSISTENTLY (not transiently) would then permanently pin the sweep at the start of its own window, blocking every id after it in the pass indefinitely. Round 2.5 (advance past the leading run of successes, stopping at the first failure's position): fixed the trailing/scattered-failure cases from round 2's regression, but a chronically-failing id that sorts FIRST in its window still pinned the sweep at that exact position forever -- Round 3's finding. The pattern across all three: any design that makes the sweep cursor's forward progress conditional on a batch's outcome can be wedged by SOME failure pattern. Only fully decoupling "the sweep always moves forward" (unconditional) from "failures are remembered and retried" (the backlog, a wholly separate mechanism) closes every variant of this bug simultaneously, which is why this patch replaced the offset logic a third time rather than patching around a fourth edge case.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test and verify_skill.py all green (govulncheck not run locally, no dependency changes); go test -race scoped to every dependent-fan-out test confirms the new failedIDs/backlog bookkeeping introduces no data race. Five end-to-end regression tests drive the real fetch/store path (not planDependentSync in isolation, which can't observe fetch failures): TestFullSyncOffsetDoesNotAdvancePastAPartialBatchFailure (round 1's original case -- a failure at the very start of the FIRST-EVER batch keeps that id pending). TestFullSyncOffsetSweepNeverWedgesOnAChronicallyFailingFirstID (round 3's exact case -- 5 ids, --max-parents 2, the first id fails on every one of 4 consecutive calls; asserts the sweep still reaches ids 3, 4, and 5 across those calls rather than staying stuck re-offering the first window). TestFullSyncOffsetFailedIDGetsBacklogPriorityAcrossCalls (a middle-of-batch chronic failure reappears FIRST -- backlog priority -- on the next call, proving it isn't silently dropped once the sweep has moved past its original position). TestPlanDependentSync_FullResumesAcrossCallsAndWrapsAfterACompletePass and TestPlanDependentSync_DryRunDoesNotPersistFullOffset (pre-existing coverage) updated to model the new plan-then-commit-on-success shape via the commitFullOffset test helper, now keyed on fullSweepCount rather than a fixed target.
